text:
It’s a privilege to serve. Pure, plentiful, affordable water is fundamental to our quality of life and key to the economic development of our community.
Maintaining our critical infrastructure is a big job, over the last 4 years we’ve made a lot of progress.
AAA Credit Rating: Mesa Water began a $70 million capital improvement program to rebuild the distribution system for the next generation. Our AAA credit rating allows us to do this.

Safe and Reliable: We have upgraded cyber security, fire hydrants and valves, reservoirs, built two new wells, replaced mainline pipes, which provide fire protection, and improved quality of life for our community.

30,000 Water Quality Tests: The system delivers over 5 billion gallons of water to 110,000 local residents and millions that travel through the service area, including John Wayne Airport. Water quality engineers complete more than 30,000 water quality tests per year to ensure our water is safe to drink.

Local Control: We advocate for local control to ensure accountability, foster local relationships, and to ensure your dollars stay local. The US Bureau of Reclamation granted the District $250K to support local Water Supply Improvement Projects.
With your vote, I’ll continue the fight for ratepayers.

text: As the owner of a small business management firm serving for profit and nonprofit organizations for over 20 years, I have dedicated my career to helping organizations manage their finances with integrity, accountability, and transparency. I will bring that same commitment to Mesa Water District.

Protecting our water supply requires responsible financial stewardship, transparent governance, and preparation for tomorrow's challenges. I support recording and publishing Board meetings, providing clear and accessible water quality information, and ensuring residents have meaningful access to district decisions.

Cybersecurity must be a top priority. Water systems across the country have become targets of increasingly sophisticated cyberattacks, making it essential that Mesa Water invests in strong cybersecurity infrastructure, regular security audits, employee training, and emergency response planning to protect our critical water systems.

I support practical investments in conservation, groundwater recharge, stormwater capture, recycled water, and water-efficient technologies to strengthen our long-term water reliability. Any future infrastructure decisions should be guided by independent science, fiscal responsibility, environmental stewardship, and the public interest.

I believe well-managed local water agencies provide the accountability and expertise our community deserves. Together, we can ensure a safe, reliable, and sustainable water future for generations to come.
